A basic Semitic word for God, often appearing alone or in compound divine names and titles.
A singular poetic form related to Elohim, used especially in elevated or wisdom-style passages.

meaning: The LORD; He is; the Self-Existent One
footnote: The covenant name of God, often represented in English Bibles as LORD in small capitals.
A poetic shortened form of the divine name, especially found in praise formulas like Hallelujah.

meaning: I AM THAT I AM; I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE
footnote: God’s self-revelation to Moses from the burning bush, emphasizing His self-existence and faithfulness.
A patriarchal divine title emphasizing God’s overwhelming power and sufficiency.

english_renderings: most high God; God most high
footnote: Title emphasizing God’s absolute supremacy over heaven, earth, kings, and nations.
Highlights God’s eternal nature and enduring covenant faithfulness.

meaning: God who sees me; God of seeing

Connects God’s revealed presence to the place where He appeared to Jacob.
A covenant formula identifying God by His faithful relationship to the patriarchs.
Continues the covenant identification of God with the patriarchal line.
A key covenant formula tying God’s present action to His promises to the fathers.
Combines the covenant name with the general divine title, stressing both God’s majesty and personal covenant relation.
A reverent title for God’s lordship, sovereignty, and authority.
A solemn compounded form often rendered Lord GOD, especially in prophetic and covenant contexts.

meaning: The LORD will provide; The LORD will see

Moses’ altar-name after victory over Amalek, portraying God as the standard and rallying point of His people.

Gideon’s altar-name after encountering God’s reassurance in fearful days.

David’s intimate confession of God’s personal guidance, provision, and care.

The closing name of Ezekiel’s restored city, centered on God’s abiding presence.
A major prophetic title, especially in Isaiah, exalting God’s transcendence and covenant holiness.

meaning: King of the universe; everlasting King
footnote: A royal title stressing God’s universal reign and eternal kingship.
A covenantal and relational address to God as Father of His people.
Daniel’s majestic vision-title for God’s eternal authority and righteous judgment.
Declares God’s sleepless covenant protection over His people.
Proclaims God as the one who vindicates, rescues, and stands for His own.
A foundational metaphor for God’s stability, faithfulness, justice, and protection.
God identifies Himself as Abram’s shield, defender, and reward.

A revelatory name declaring God’s presence with His people, ultimately fulfilled in Christ.
A striking messianic divine title that directly attributes deity and strength.
A throne title in the messianic prophecy emphasizing eternal care and rule.
A messianic royal title pointing to the divine ruler who brings true peace.

Applied to Christ as the perfect visible revelation of the invisible God.
